Rashi on Nedarim 5a:1:1.english: However, if he said “I am avowed from you” alone - That he did not say: “That which I eat of yours.”

Rashi on Nedarim 5a:1:2.hebrew: שניהן אסורין - דכיון דאמר ״שאני אוכל לך״, משמע דאסר נפשיה בלבד, שאינו אוכל מחבירו. אבל כי אמר ״מודרני הימך״ סתם, משמע דמדיר נמי חבריה מיניה, מכל וכל:
Rashi on Nedarim 5a:1:2.english: They are both prohibited - For when he says: “That I eat of yours,” it implies that he prohibited only himself, that he does not eat benefiting from his fellow; but when he says: “I am avowed from you” without specification, it implies that he also prohibits his fellow from benefiting from him entirely.

Rashi on Nedarim 5a:2:1.english: We learned - In the chapter [entitled] Hashuttafin (below 47b).

Rashi on Nedarim 5a:2:2.hebrew: הריני עליך חרם המודר אסור - והא הכא, דלא אמר ״שאני אוכל לך חרם״, ולא הוי אסור אלא המודר, ולא שניהן:
Rashi on Nedarim 5a:2:2.english: "I am hereby to you cherem," the one avowed is prohibited - And behold here, where he did not say "that which I eat of yours is cherem," and only the one avowed is prohibited, and not both of them.

Rashi on Nedarim 5a:2:3.hebrew: כגון דמפריש - בהדיא: ״אבל את עלי לא״:
Rashi on Nedarim 5a:2:3.english: Such as where he specifies - Explicitly: “But you are not [forbidden] to me.”

Rashi on Nedarim 5a:4:1.hebrew: אבל סתמא - דלא פריש ״ואת עלי לא״ — מאי? שניהן אסורין:
Rashi on Nedarim 5a:4:1.english: But [in] an unspecified [case] - Where he did not specify, "And you are not [prohibited] to me" — what [is the law]? Both of them are prohibited.

Rashi on Nedarim 5a:4:2.hebrew: הדין הוא דשניהן אסורין - דאמר בפירוש: ״הריני עליך ואת עלי״. אבל סתמא, דאמר: ״הריני עליך״ ולא אמר ״ואת עלי״ — לא הוו שניהן אסורין, אלא חד בלבד:
Rashi on Nedarim 5a:4:2.english: It is in this case that both are prohibited - Where he said explicitly: “I am hereby to you, and you are to me.” But in an unspecified case, where he said: “I am hereby to you,” and did not say: “and you are to me,” both of them would not be prohibited, but only one of them.

Rashi on Nedarim 5a:5:1.hebrew: אלא הכי איתמר אמר ר' יוסי בר' חנינא מודרני ממך הוא אסור וכו' - דהיינו כמתניתין: ״הריני עליך חרם וכו'״:
Rashi on Nedarim 5a:5:1.english: Rather, this is how it was stated: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said: “I am avowed from you,” he is prohibited, etc. - That is, like our Mishnah: “I am hereby to you cherem, etc.”

Rashi on Nedarim 5a:6:1.hebrew: והא מתני' מודרני הימך - קתני, ואוקמא שמואל דאמר בכולן עם כל אחד ואחד "שאני אוכל", דאהכי איהו אסור וחבירו מותר. אבל אמר "מודרני הימך" בלבד ולא אמר "שאני אוכל" — שניהן אסורין, והיינו דלא כרבי יוסי בר' חנינא:
Rashi on Nedarim 5a:6:1.english: And doesn't the Mishnah state: "I am avowed from you" - The Mishnah teaches this, and Shmuel established it as referring to a case where he said in all of them, with each and every one, "that I eat," for because of this he is prohibited and his fellow is permitted. But if he said only "I am avowed from you," and did not say "that I eat," both of them are prohibited. And this is not in accordance with Rabbi Yose beRabbi Chanina.

Rashi on Nedarim 5a:7:1.hebrew: אלא מעיקרא דשמואל הכי איתמר - הכי מתרץ לה למתניתין, ולא כדאוקימנא, דתיקשי לר' יוסי:
Rashi on Nedarim 5a:7:1.english: Rather, this is how the opinion of Shmuel was originally stated - This is how he resolves the Mishnah, and not as we established it earlier, so that it would pose a difficulty to Rabbi Yosei.

Rashi on Nedarim 5a:7:2.hebrew: הא אמר מודרני הימך - דלא מפרש כלום, ודאי מכולה מילתא מדיר, ואסור אפי' בהנאה:
Rashi on Nedarim 5a:7:2.english: However, [if] he said: “I am avowed from you” - Since he did not specify anything, he certainly vows [himself off] from everything, and is forbidden even from [deriving] benefit.

Rashi on Nedarim 5a:8:1.hebrew: א"ה לימא שמואל הכי - למה ליה אפושי למימריה כולי האי? לימא: הכי אמר שמואל, ואם לא אמר "שאני אוכל לך" — דלא אמר אלא "מודרני הימך" — אסור אפילו בהנאה:
Rashi on Nedarim 5a:8:1.english: If so, let Shmuel say as follows - Why did he need to lengthen his statement so much? Let him say: Thus said Shmuel: "And if he did not say 'that which I eat of yours' — [meaning] that he said only 'I am avowed from you' — he is prohibited even from [deriving] benefit."

Rashi on Nedarim 5a:9:1.hebrew: אלא הכי אתמר - אמר שמואל: טעמא דאמר ״שאני אוכל לך״ — דכיון דאמר בפירוש אכילה, אסור; אבל לא אמר בפירוש אכילה — לא אסור למיכל מדידיה, דדילמא הא דאמר ״מודר אני ממך״ אדיבוריה קאמר, דלא מישתעי בהדיה, אבל לא למיכל מיניה. וכן כי אמר ״מופרשני ממך״ דלא אמר ״שאני אוכל״ — דדילמא ממשא ומתן קא פריש מיניה. ״מרוחקני ממך״ נמי — דלא ליקרב בארבע אמות דיליה משמע, ולא דמדיר מאכילתו:
Rashi on Nedarim 5a:9:1.english: Rather, this is how it was stated - Shmuel said: The reason he is forbidden is that he said: “That which I eat of yours,” for since he explicitly stated eating, he is forbidden. But if he did not explicitly state eating, he is not forbidden to eat of his food, for perhaps that which he said: “I am avowed from you,” he stated regarding his speech, that he will not speak with him, but not to prohibit himself from eating from him. And similarly when he said: “I am separated from you,” where he did not say: “That which I eat,” for perhaps he is separating from him from business. “I am distanced from you” as well indicates that he will not approach within his four cubits, and not that he vows against his food.

Tosafot on Nedarim 5a:2:1.hebrew: תנן הריני עליך חרם המודר אסור אבל לא המדיר - ולשמואל דאמר: "מודרני ממך" משמע תרוייהו, הכי נמי נימא: "הריני עליך חרם" משמע "הריני על ממונך חרם", וגם מדיר נמי ליתסר? ומשני: דפריש "ואת עלי לא". ועתה פריך: "הרי את עלי חרם" — אסור ומודר מותר; ואמאי? נימא דה"ק: "הרי את עלי וממוני חרם", ואסור גם מודר:
Tosafot on Nedarim 5a:2:1.english: We learned: "I am hereby to you cherem; the one avowed is prohibited, but not the one who made the vow" - And according to Shmuel, who said that "I am avowed from you" implies both of them, here too let us say that "I am hereby to you cherem" implies "I am cherem upon your property," and let the one who made the vow also be prohibited! And [the Gemara] answers that [it is a case] where he specified: "And you are not [cherem] to me." And now [the Gemara] objects: [If he said,] "You are hereby to me cherem," [the one who made the vow] is prohibited and the one avowed is permitted; but why? Let us say that this is what he is saying: "You are [cherem] to me, and my property is cherem [to you]," and let the one avowed also be prohibited!

Tosafot on Nedarim 5a:5:1.hebrew: אלא אי איתמר דרבי יוסי בר חנינא הכי אתמר מודר אני ממך הוא אסור וחבירו מותר - תימה: מאי אתא לאשמעי'? הא תנא בברייתא הכי! וי"ל, דאשמעי' ד"מודרני ממך" לא משמע מודר ממונו; אע"ג ד"הריני חרם" ר"ל מודר ממונו — זה לא אמר הכי:
Tosafot on Nedarim 5a:5:1.english: "Rather, if [the statement] of Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina was stated, it was stated like this: 'I am avowed from you' — he is prohibited and his fellow is permitted" - [This is] puzzling: What did [Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina] come to teach us? Behold, [the Tanna already] taught this in a baraita! And one can say that it teaches us that "I am avowed from you" does not imply that [the other is] prohibited from his property; even though [saying] "I am hereby dedicated" means [that the other is] prohibited from his property, this [speaker] did not say so.

Tosafot on Nedarim 5a:6:1.hebrew: והא מתני' דממך תנן - כלומר: אכתי [קשה], דשמואל קאמר דאמר "דמודרני ממך" — דשניהם אסורים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 5a:6:1.english: "But didn't we learn in the Mishnah: 'From you'?" - That is to say, it is still [difficult], as Shmuel stated that [if] one said, "I am avowed from you," both are prohibited.

Tosafot on Nedarim 5a:7:1.hebrew: אלא שמואל הכי אתמר טעמא דאמר שאני אוכל הוא דאין אסור אלא באכילה - דלישנא ד"אסור" במתני' משמע ליה: אסור באכילה ולא בהנאה; אבל "מודרני ממך" — אסור בהנאה, ומודרני דקתני בברייתא — אסור בהנאה. וה"ק שמואל: וכולן אסור בהנאה, עד שיאמר "שאני טועם לך":
Tosafot on Nedarim 5a:7:1.english: "Rather, this is how [the statement of] Shmuel was stated: The reason is that he said, 'That which I eat,' [it is for this reason] that he is prohibited only from eating" - For the expression "prohibited" in the Mishnah implied to him [that he is] prohibited from eating, and not from deriving benefit; but [if one said,] "I am avowed from you," he is prohibited from deriving benefit. And [in the case of] "I am avowed [from you]" that is taught in the baraita, he is [likewise] prohibited from deriving benefit. And this is what Shmuel was saying: And in all of them, he is prohibited from deriving benefit, until [i.e., unless] he says: "That which I taste of yours."

Tosafot on Nedarim 5a:8:1.hebrew: אי הכי לימא שמואל הכי אם לא אמר שאני טועם לך אסור [אפי'] בהנאה - דלישנא "עד שיאמר שאני טועם לך" משמע: כשאני טועם אסר עצמו טפי ממודרני; והא ליתא, דאדרבה, מודרני חמור טפי. ויש ספרים דגרסי: "לימא שמואל: ואם לא אמר אלא שאני אוכל לך, אינו אסור אלא באכילה", וקשה ליישבו. וה"ה דלעיל, דשמואל קאמר "אבל מודרני שניהם אסורים", מצי למפרך: לימא שמואל "אם לא אמר שאני אוכל לך, שניהם אסורים":
Tosafot on Nedarim 5a:8:1.english: "If so, let Shmuel say as follows: If he did not say: 'That which I taste of yours,' he is prohibited [even] from benefit" - For the phrasing "until he says: 'That which I taste of yours'" implies that by [saying] "that which I taste," he prohibited himself more than [by saying] "I am avowed [from you]"; but this is not so, for on the contrary, "I am avowed" is more stringent. And there are books that read: "Let Shmuel say: 'And if he said only: That which I eat of yours, he is prohibited only from eating,'" and it is difficult to explain it. And the same applies to above, where Shmuel says: "However, [in the case of] 'I am avowed,' both are prohibited" — [the Gemara] could have objected: Let Shmuel say: "If he did not say: 'That which I eat of yours,' both are prohibited."

Tosafot on Nedarim 5a:9:1.hebrew: אלא הכי איתמר - לעולם כדאמר מעיקרא: דלשמואל מודרני לחודיה לא אסר כלל, דלמא לא משתעי בהדך קאמר. וקשה מברייתא דלעיל: דמודרני אסור בלא שאני טועם לך! וי"ל, דהאי אסור — ר"ל דלא מישתעי בהדיה. א"נ, מעתה נחית לומר: תנאי היא, דברייתא דלעיל ס"ל כרבנן, דידים שאינם מוכיחות הויין ידים; ושמואל סבר דמתני' כרבי יהודה, דאמר לא הויין ידים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 5a:9:1.english: Rather, this is how it was stated - Actually, [the explanation is] as it said originally: that according to Shmuel, "I am avowed" by itself does not prohibit anything at all, for perhaps he meant "I am not speaking with you." And [this] is difficult from the baraita mentioned above, [which stated] that "I am avowed" is prohibited without "that I taste of yours"! And one can say that this [word] "prohibited" means that he may not speak with him. Alternatively, from now on [the Gemara] proceeds to say that it is a dispute between Tannaim: for the baraita above holds in accordance with the Rabbis, that ambiguous intimations are [valid] intimations; and Shmuel holds that the Mishnah is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, who said [that they] are not [valid] intimations.
